title: Grateful Dead Live at Strand Lyceum on 1972-05-23
source: uncertain (believed to be 10" 2-track reel master>1 cassette generation>DAT> 1 cassette generation>circulation

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy May ’72 show with a smoking Dark Star, stellar Two Souls in Communion and multiple tour‑classic performances.
ai_review.review: The recording is widely praised for its clarity—despite some tape hiss it sounds crisp and well‑balanced, essentially a top‑tier soundboard transfer. Musically the concert delivers a powerhouse first set and an adventurous second set highlighted by an extended Dark Star, a soaring Morning Dew, and standout renditions of Two Souls in Communion, Mr. Charlie and Hey Bo Diddley. Overall the band is tight, energetic and the performance is regarded as one of the tour’s finest.

ai_rating.rationale: Multiple 5‑star reviews praise both the musical intensity and the sound quality; only minor recording quirks are noted, leading to a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with remastered clarity; occasional tape hiss noted but it recedes quickly and does not detract from listenability.

standout_songs: China Cat > I’m a King Bee (Rider)
Sitting On Top of the World
Rockin' Pneumonia & The Boogie Woogie Flu
Hey Bo Diddley / Not Fade Away suite
poor_songs: Dark Star (second‑set opening – described as static)
Uncle John's Band (tightness lost toward the end)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A long, laid‑back first set that builds momentum with classic blues and rock numbers; the second set opens a bit static but quickly lifts with an exploratory Dark Star leading into a powerful Morning Dew, followed by high‑energy closers that keep the excitement high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s bending, sustained notes and organ work are highlighted; praised for his tone on Dark Star, guitar brilliance on Two Souls, and surprising organ playing on Good Lovin’.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s rumbling bass is noted as a strong foundation during the Dark Star jam.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal contributions (e.g., Jack Straw) and interplay with Garcia receive positive mentions; occasional teasing noted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux praised for rag‑time feel on Chinatown Shuffle and overall keyboard texture; Pigpen’s organ on Two Souls is called quintessential.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s tom work described as “devilish” and his drumming sections are highlighted as driving forces in the improvisations.
